planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in shade to partial shade; Faith is a sister seedling to 'Charity', raised from open-pollinated 'Charity' seed at Windsor Great Park and named by Christopher Brickell.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in shade to deep partial shade, tolerating heavier shade than most flowering evergreen shrubs. Faith is a sister seedling of the classic 'Charity', raised at Windsor Great Park from open-pollinated 'Charity' seed and named alongside its sibling 'Hope', leaning closer to Mahonia lomariifolia in habit and foliage than 'Charity' does, with softly colored, fragrant yellow flower spikes held above bold, holly-like evergreen foliage in late fall and winter, followed by tart blue-black berries. Its architectural form and off-season bloom give it strong winter garden value when little else is flowering. Water during establishment and dry spells, and prune only to remove dead or leggy canes.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in shade to partial shade; Hope is a sister seedling to 'Charity' and 'Faith', raised from open-pollinated 'Charity' seed at Windsor Great Park.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in shade to deep partial shade, tolerating heavier shade than most flowering evergreen shrubs. Hope is a sister seedling of 'Charity' and 'Faith', raised at Windsor Great Park from open-pollinated 'Charity' seed, bearing fragrant yellow flower racemes from January into March above bold, holly-like evergreen foliage, followed by powdery blue-black berries. It is a somewhat more compact, cold-hardy selection than most other Mahonia x media clones, useful where a smaller-scale winter-flowering shade shrub is wanted. Water during establishment and dry spells, and prune only to remove dead or leggy canes.

common_name: Orange Flame Mahonia (Orange-Red New Growth Oregon Grape)

planting.note: Plant container stock or bare-root plants in spring or fall in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, moderately fertile soil in part shade to full shade, tolerating more sun than most mahonias; Orange Flame (Plant Patent 2544) is grown chiefly for its vividly colored new foliage.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic, moderately fertile soil in part shade to full shade, avoiding exposed sites with harsh winter wind. Orange Flame is a patented Oregon grape selection prized for its striking new growth, which emerges vivid orange-red before aging to glossy green through summer and turning wine-red again in fall and winter. Clusters of bright yellow flowers open in spring, followed by dusty, glaucous-blue, tart, edible berries on the same spiny, holly-like evergreen foliage typical of the species. Its multi-season color makes it a strong accent in a shaded shrub border. Prune only to remove dead or leggy canes at ground level.

planting.note: Plant container stock or bare-root plants in spring or fall in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral, moderately fertile soil in part shade to full shade, tolerating more sun than most mahonias in cooler climates; Smaragd (German/Scandinavian for 'emerald') is a dense, compact selection.

directions: Plant in well-drained, slightly acidic, moderately fertile soil in part shade to full shade, avoiding exposed sites with harsh winter wind and afternoon sun. Smaragd is a dense, low-mounding Oregon grape selection staying under 2 feet tall, with bronze new foliage maturing to deep glossy green through summer and turning purple-red in winter. Dense clusters of yellow flowers open in spring, followed by dusty blue-black, tart, edible berries on spiny, holly-like evergreen leaves. Its compact scale suits foreground plantings in a shaded shrub border or as a flowering groundcover under high shade. Prune only to remove dead or leggy canes at ground level.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in fall or spring in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in shade to partial shade; Home Wood is an upright, columnar Mahonia x media selection with dramatic pinnate leaves to 28 inches long.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in shade to deep partial shade, tolerating heavier shade than most flowering evergreen shrubs. Home Wood is a large, upright, columnar Mahonia x media selection with dramatic, boldly pinnate leaves reaching nearly two and a half feet long, and slightly fragrant yellow flowers carried in ascending clusters up to 14 inches tall in late autumn and winter, followed by blue-black berries. Its imposing architectural scale makes it best suited to a spacious shaded border or woodland-edge planting rather than a tight foundation bed. Water during establishment and dry spells, and prune only to remove dead or leggy canes.

common_name: Sweet Winter Mahonia (Minganpi Compact Thornless Mahonia)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in fall or early spring in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Sweet Winter (sold under the breeder name 'Minganpi') is an upright, compact, spine-free selection distinct from 'Soft Caress' and 'Marvel'.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade. Sweet Winter is an upright, compact, spine-free Mahonia eurybracteata selection with narrow, linear-lanceolate leaflets that emerge bronze and mature dark green, distinct in habit and leaf shape from the similarly thornless 'Soft Caress' and 'Marvel'. Lightly fragrant, bright yellow flower racemes open along the stem tips from autumn into winter, followed by small, blue-black, powdery-coated berries. It thrives in deep shade under tree canopies where few other flowering shrubs perform well. Water during establishment and dry spells, and prune only to remove dead or leggy canes.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Dentata is a female selection grown for its dark green, glossy, distinctly toothed foliage rather than variegation.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade. Dentata is a female Aucuba japonica selection grown for its dark green, glossy, distinctly toothed leaves rather than for variegation, giving it a coarser, more serrated texture than the plain-leaved species. Small purple flowers open in mid-spring, followed by showy red berries in winter when a male aucuba is nearby for pollination. Like other aucubas, it is one of the few broadleaf evergreen shrubs that thrives in deep, dry shade under trees, making it valuable for difficult shaded foundation plantings and understory beds. Little pruning is needed beyond removing damaged or leggy stems in spring.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Fujikawa is a female selection with unusually narrow, pointed leaves that are sometimes lobed at the tip, unlike any other widely grown aucuba cultivar.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, avoiding direct sun. Fujikawa is a distinctive female Aucuba japonica selection with extremely narrow, pointed, glossy green leaves to about 8 inches long and only about 1 inch wide, occasionally forming one or two lobes near the tip — a texture unlike any other widely available aucuba cultivar, giving the plant an almost tropical, palm-like appearance. It reaches roughly 4 feet tall and wide over five to seven years. Female plants produce red, marble-sized berries in winter if a male aucuba is nearby for pollination. Like other aucubas, it thrives in deep, dry shade under trees where little else stays attractive. Little pruning is needed beyond removing damaged or leggy stems in spring.
